questions.q:
With reference to PM Vishwakarma, consider the following statements:
1. It offers collateral-free loans of up to Rs 3 lakh in two tranches.
2. Beneficiaries pay a concessional interest of 5 per cent, with the Government bearing subvention of up to 8 per cent.
3. More than one member of a family can register and receive benefits.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; only one member per family (spouses and unmarried children) can register. The first tranche is up to Rs 1 lakh for 18 months and the second up to Rs 2 lakh for 30 months. The scheme reached its target of 30 lakh registrations, with 6.19 lakh loans worth about Rs 5,316 crore sanctioned.

questions.q: Under PM Vishwakarma, applications are accepted
o: only on the Udyam portal by self-registration
questions.e: Registration is only through CSCs, followed by three-tier verification: Gram Panchayat or Urban Local Body, then the District Implementation Committee, then the Screening Committee. Beneficiaries get a certificate and ID card and are onboarded on the Udyam Assist Platform as formal micro enterprises.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
PM Vishwakarma component : Benefit
1. Toolkit incentive : Up to Rs 15,000
2. Skill training stipend : Rs 500 per day
3. Digital incentive : Rs 10 per transaction, up to 1,000 transactions a month
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The digital incentive is Rs 1 per digital payment or receipt, up to 100 transactions a month. Basic training lasts 5-7 days and advanced training 15 days or more. The scheme's three pillars are Samman, Samarthya and Samriddhi.

questions.q:
Which of the following are among the 18 trades covered under PM Vishwakarma?
1. Boat maker
2. Armourer
3. Weaver of handloom silk sarees
4. Fishing-net maker
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Boat makers, armourers and fishing-net makers are among the 18 trades, along with carpenters, blacksmiths, goldsmiths, potters, cobblers, masons, barbers, tailors, washermen and garland makers. Handloom weaving is not listed; the list includes basket, mat and broom makers and coir weavers.

questions.q:
With reference to the eligibility rules of PM Vishwakarma, consider the following statements:
1. Government employees and their family members are not eligible.
2. MUDRA and PM SVANidhi borrowers who have fully repaid their loans are eligible.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Applicants must be at least 18, self-employed in the unorganised sector in one of the 18 family-based trades, and must not have taken similar self-employment loans in the previous five years. The scheme was launched on Vishwakarma Jayanti, 17 September 2023, under the MSME ministry.
